framework.title: BRACE and the NIST AI RMF

mappings.name: Legal and regulatory duties for AI are known, managed, and written down.
mappings.rationale: E11 keeps audit records as long as the law requires; every other legal duty is outside BRACE.

mappings.name: Trustworthy-AI traits are built into organizational policies and practices.
mappings.rationale: The gates give a release rule for security and accountability only; the policy itself and the other traits are organizational work.

mappings.name: The organization decides how much risk management each system needs, based on its risk tolerance.
mappings.rationale: The stakes and autonomy rating decides when Detection items must pass; setting the organization's tolerance happens outside BRACE.

mappings.name: The risk process and its results are set by clear policies and controls based on risk priorities.
mappings.rationale: Each release has written pass rules and a recorded result, but the organization-wide process is not BRACE's.

mappings.name: Monitoring and periodic review of the risk process are planned, with roles and review frequency set.
mappings.rationale: BRACE sets a next review date, reopen triggers, and an owner per item for one agent, not for the whole risk program.

mappings.name: There is a way to inventory AI systems.
mappings.rationale: The manifest, type ID, and lookup drill describe each agent; keeping a list of all AI systems is organizational work.

mappings.name: AI systems can be retired safely.
mappings.rationale: Revoking access, stopping sub-agents, and leaving work in a safe state support retirement, but BRACE has no retirement process.

mappings.name: Roles, duties, and lines of communication for AI risk are written down and clear.
mappings.rationale: Every action names an accountable party and owner, and each control has a named owner on both sides; organization-wide roles are outside BRACE.

mappings.name: Staff and partners get AI risk training.
mappings.rationale: BRACE does not cover training.

mappings.name: Executive leaders take responsibility for AI risk decisions.
mappings.rationale: BRACE names who approves release and who accepts each risk; making that person an executive is the organization's choice.

mappings.name: Risk decisions are informed by a diverse team.
mappings.rationale: Team diversity is a workforce matter.

mappings.name: Policies define roles for human-AI setups and oversight.
mappings.rationale: BRACE records who may approve high-impact actions and who may stop the agent; the wider policy is organizational.

mappings.name: Policies build a critical-thinking, safety-first culture.
mappings.rationale: Culture is an organizational matter.

mappings.name: Teams write down AI risks and impacts and share them more widely.
mappings.rationale: BRACE records the worst credible damage, the risky capability combination, and accepted exposure; wider impacts and sharing are not covered.

mappings.name: Practices support AI testing, finding incidents, and sharing information.
mappings.rationale: Release tests, security alerts, and an incident drill with a named reporting decision cover one agent; organization-wide practice is outside BRACE.

mappings.name: Feedback from people outside the team about social impacts is gathered and used.
mappings.rationale: BRACE does not collect outside feedback on impacts.

mappings.name: The team regularly folds reviewed outside feedback into design.
mappings.rationale: BRACE does not cover feedback from AI actors.

mappings.name: Policies cover third-party AI risks, including intellectual property.
mappings.rationale: BRACE vets, pins, and assigns owners to third-party parts; intellectual property and the policy itself are outside BRACE.

mappings.name: There are backup plans for failures or incidents in high-risk third-party data or AI.
mappings.rationale: A drill handles a compromised shared tool, model changes have pause rules, gateways fail closed, and rollback is tested.

mappings.name: Purpose, uses, laws, users, settings, and possible impacts are written down.
mappings.rationale: The deployment record covers task, setting, tenants, data, actions, autonomy, and worst damage, but not laws or wider social impact.

mappings.name: Diverse, cross-field people help set the context, and that is recorded.
mappings.rationale: Team makeup is a workforce matter.

mappings.name: The organization's mission and AI goals are written down.
mappings.rationale: Mission is set by the organization.

mappings.name: The business value of the system is defined.
mappings.rationale: BRACE does not judge business value.

mappings.name: The organization's risk tolerances are set and written down.
mappings.rationale: The gates fix what blocks release and need approved risk acceptance for gaps; overall tolerance is set by the organization.

mappings.name: System requirements are gathered, and design accounts for social and technical effects.
mappings.rationale: BRACE supplies security requirements for the agent; other requirements, such as user privacy promises, need separate work.

mappings.name: The tasks the system supports and the methods it uses are defined.
mappings.rationale: The deployment record names the task, each tool has a task reason, and the manifest lists every model.

mappings.name: The system's knowledge limits and how people oversee its output are written down.
mappings.rationale: BRACE documents approval and stop points; it does not document what the model knows or doesn't know.

mappings.name: Scientific soundness and test, evaluation, verification, and validation (TEVV) needs are written down, including data choices.
mappings.rationale: BRACE sets up security tests and records dataset versions, but not data quality or construct validity.

mappings.name: Possible benefits are examined and written down.
mappings.rationale: BRACE does not assess benefits.

mappings.name: Possible costs of AI errors, tied to risk tolerance, are examined and written down.
mappings.rationale: BRACE records worst credible damage and the exposure of each accepted gap; it does not cost out ordinary errors.

mappings.name: The system's intended scope is set and written down.
mappings.rationale: The allowed task, tools, permissions, and reachable systems are written down and enforced.

mappings.name: Operator skill with the system, and related standards, are defined and checked.
mappings.rationale: Drills show operators can stop, find, and contain the agent; training and certification are outside BRACE.

mappings.name: Human oversight processes are defined, checked, and written down.
mappings.rationale: High-impact actions need tested approvals, a named person can stop the agent, and alerts reach a named responder.

mappings.name: Technical and legal risks of all parts, including third-party ones, are mapped.
mappings.rationale: BRACE vets each part's source, publisher, and known flaws; legal and intellectual property risks are not covered.

mappings.name: Internal risk controls for each part, including third-party AI, are written down.
mappings.rationale: Every outside part and model is listed, with the controls that apply and an owner on each side.

mappings.name: The likelihood and size of each impact are written down.
mappings.rationale: BRACE records worst credible damage and accepted exposure; it does not rate likelihood or helpful impacts.

mappings.name: People and practices are in place to gather feedback about impacts.
mappings.rationale: BRACE does not cover engagement with affected people.

mappings.name: Methods and metrics are chosen for the biggest risks first, and unmeasured risks are noted.
mappings.rationale: BRACE sets measurable targets and records what each check can't prove, but only for security risks.

mappings.name: Metrics and controls are reviewed and updated, including error reports and community impact.
mappings.rationale: Controls are re-tested each release and detection miss rates are measured; community impact is not covered.

mappings.name: Experts who did not build the system, or independent assessors, take part in reviews.
mappings.rationale: BRACE requires named reviewers, but it does not require them to be independent of the builders.

mappings.name: Test sets, metrics, and test tools are written down.
mappings.rationale: Security tests record fixtures, targets, tester, date, and setup differences; quality tests are outside BRACE.

mappings.name: Tests with human subjects meet protection rules and represent the population.
mappings.rationale: BRACE does not run tests on people.

mappings.name: Performance or assurance criteria are measured in conditions like real use.
mappings.rationale: Release candidates are tested through the real harness, with measured stop and revocation times and recorded setup differences.

mappings.name: The system and its parts are watched in production.
mappings.rationale: BRACE watches actions, drift, and security signals; it keeps answer quality out of scope.

mappings.name: The system is shown to be valid and reliable, with limits noted.
mappings.rationale: BRACE does not test whether the agent's answers are correct.

mappings.name: The system is tested for safety, stays within risk tolerance, and fails safely.
mappings.rationale: BRACE tests safe stopping, blocked high-impact actions, and hard limits; it does not test harmful content or other safety risks.

mappings.name: Security and resilience are evaluated and written down.
mappings.rationale: Attack cases, bypass tests, and recovery tests run against each release candidate, and the results are kept.

mappings.name: Transparency and accountability risks are examined and written down.
mappings.rationale: Every action can be traced to an agent, owner, and tenant; transparency to users is not covered.

mappings.name: The model is explained, validated, and documented, and output is read in context.
mappings.rationale: BRACE documents which models ran and what they did; it does not explain or validate the model.

mappings.name: Privacy risk is examined and written down.
mappings.rationale: BRACE tests leakage and tenant separation; a full privacy risk review is outside BRACE.

mappings.name: Fairness and bias are evaluated.
mappings.rationale: BRACE does not test fairness or bias.

mappings.name: Environmental impact is assessed.
mappings.rationale: BRACE does not measure environmental impact.

mappings.name: The test methods themselves are checked for how well they work.
mappings.rationale: BRACE measures detector misses and false alarms and repeats attacks; other test methods are not reviewed.

mappings.name: People and methods are in place to track known and new risks over time.
mappings.rationale: Monitoring, provider notices, and review triggers track security risks; other risks need separate tracking.

mappings.name: Risk tracking is planned for risks that are hard to measure.
mappings.rationale: Fallbacks record what is uncertain and who owns it, but only for security risks.

mappings.name: Users and affected people can report problems and appeal outcomes.
mappings.rationale: BRACE has no user feedback or appeal process.

mappings.name: Measurement fits the real setting and draws on domain experts and users.
mappings.rationale: Tests run on the real release and record setup differences; consulting experts and users is outside BRACE.

mappings.name: Experts and AI actors help confirm the system works as intended.
mappings.rationale: BRACE does not check intended performance with experts.

mappings.name: Gains or drops in performance are found through consultation and field data.
mappings.rationale: BRACE does not track performance with affected communities.

mappings.name: A decision is made on whether the system meets its goals and should go ahead.
mappings.rationale: BRACE supplies security evidence, gaps and unknowns. High-risk reports carry no BRACE release verdict; accountable people own any deployment decision and gradual monitored rollout. Whether the agent meets its goals is judged elsewhere.

mappings.name: Risk treatment is prioritized by impact, likelihood, and resources.
mappings.rationale: Gates and the stakes rating set fixed priorities for security gaps; they do not weigh likelihood or cost.

mappings.name: Responses to high-priority risks are planned and written down (reduce, transfer, avoid, or accept).
mappings.rationale: Each security gap gets a fix, a cut in powers, or an approved acceptance with an owner; other risks are not covered.

mappings.name: Leftover risks to buyers and end users are written down.
mappings.rationale: Accepted gaps record their exposure and compensating controls; telling buyers and users is outside BRACE.

mappings.name: Resources and non-AI alternatives are considered to reduce impact.
mappings.rationale: BRACE does not compare AI with non-AI options.

mappings.name: There are ways to keep a deployed system's value over time.
mappings.rationale: Drift checks, model-change controls, and rollback keep the approved setup running; value is not measured.

mappings.name: There are steps to respond to and recover from a newly found risk.
mappings.rationale: A tested incident drill, rollback, checked recovery, and safe-state steps handle new problems.

mappings.name: There are ways, with named owners, to replace, disengage, or shut off a system that misbehaves.
mappings.rationale: A named person can stop the agent and its sub-agents within a tested time and cut off its access.

mappings.name: Third-party risks and benefits are watched, and controls are applied and written down.
mappings.rationale: Tools and models are re-checked on load and watched for flaws; third-party benefits and non-security risks are outside BRACE.

mappings.name: Pre-trained models are watched as part of regular upkeep.
mappings.rationale: Every model is pinned or tracked, changes trigger re-tests, and the running model is checked against the manifest.

mappings.name: Post-deployment monitoring covers user input, appeals and overrides, retirement, incidents, recovery, and change.
mappings.rationale: BRACE covers monitoring, override, incidents, recovery, and change review; user input and appeals are not covered.

mappings.name: Measurable improvements are built into updates, with input from interested parties.
mappings.rationale: Each release is re-tested and gaps are tracked to an owner; engagement with interested parties is outside BRACE.

mappings.name: Incidents are shared with affected parties, and handled and recorded.
mappings.rationale: BRACE records what happened and names who decides on outside reporting; telling affected communities is outside BRACE.
